title: Neijuan
summary: Neijuan (内卷) is a Chinese sociological concept meaning 'involution' that describes a phenomenon where individuals in a competitive system work increasingly harder against each other, but no one ultimately benefits, resembling a zero-sum game or rat race. The term gained widespread popularity in China starting around 2020 to describe hyper-competitive environments in education, employment, and society where excessive competition produces diminishing returns for all participants.
problem_solved: Describes and names the problem of unproductive hyper-competition where everyone works harder but no one benefits.
why_valuable: Provides a conceptual framework for understanding and discussing unsustainable competitive pressures in modern society, particularly relevant to education and职场 cultures.
